title: Forward scan — finding earliest start times
problem:
A project has the following activities. Perform a forward scan to find the EST and EFT of each activity.

| Activity | Predecessors | Duration (days) |
|---|---|---|
| A | — | 4 |
| B | — | 6 |
| C | A | 3 |
| D | A, B | 5 |
| E | C, D | 2 |

steps.working: For activities with no predecessors, EST = 0. For all others, EST = maximum of the EFTs of all immediate predecessors. EFT = EST + duration.

steps.instruction: Find the EST and EFT of A and B, which have no predecessors.
Find the EST and EFT of C, which follows A only.
Find the EST and EFT of D, which follows both A and B.
steps.working:
D must wait for the later finish of its predecessors.
$$\text{EST}_D = \max(\text{EFT}_A,\ \text{EFT}_B) = \max(4, 6) = 6,\quad \text{EFT}_D = 6 + 5 = 11$$

steps.instruction: Find the EST and EFT of E, which follows both C and D.

answer: The minimum project completion time is the EFT of the last activity: 13 days.

title: Backward scan — finding latest start times
problem: Using the same project from Example 1 (minimum duration = 13 days), perform a backward scan to find the LST of each activity.

steps.working: For the last activity, LST = project duration − duration of that activity. For all others, LST = minimum of the LSTs of all immediate successors, minus this activity's duration.

steps.instruction: Find the LST of E, the last activity.
Find the LST of D, for which only E follows.
Find the LST of C, for which only E follows.
Find the LST of B, for which only D follows.
Find the LST of A, for which both C and D follow — take the minimum.

answer: LST values: A = 2, B = 0, C = 8, D = 6, E = 11.

title: Calculating float
problem: Using the ESTs from Example 1 and LSTs from Example 2, calculate the float of each activity and identify which have zero float. Float = LST − EST. An activity with float = 0 is on the critical path.

steps.instruction: Tabulate EST and LST for each activity and compute the float.
Identify the activities with zero float.
steps.working: Activities B, D and E all have float = 0. These are on the critical path.

steps.instruction: Note the float of the non-critical activities.
steps.working: Activity A has 2 days of float — it can start up to 2 days late without delaying the project. Activity C has 4 days of float.

steps.instruction: State the critical path and confirm its total duration.
steps.working: The critical path is B → D → E, with total duration $6 + 5 + 2 = 13$ days, confirming the minimum project time.

answer: The critical path is B → D → E (float = 0), with total duration 13 days.
